title: Python Mastery
blurb: From names and references to decorators, generators, the data model, typing, asyncio and CPython internals: the Python you need to read, write and defend in an interview.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 1-2
Matthes, Python Crash Course (3rd ed.), Parts I-II (topic coverage; all wording and examples original)
The Python Tutorial, Language Reference (Data Model) and Library Reference, docs.python.org/3

title: The Linux Command Line
blurb: From your first prompt to shell scripts, text pipelines and on-call debugging: the command line explained from the ground up, with Python problems that rebuild the classic tools.
sources: Shotts, The Linux Command Line (5th internet edition)
Original material on ssh, tmux, curl, jq, git, cron, systemd, GPUs and Docker

title: Git (Pro Git)
blurb: Git from first commit to object internals: branching, rebasing, remotes, GitHub flow, history surgery and rescue drills, with Python problems that rebuild the commit graph, diff, merge and reflog yourself.
sources: Chacon & Straub, Pro Git, 2nd edition (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), chapters 1-10
Original material on team workflows, commit conventions and rescue scenarios

title: Practical Vim
blurb: tmp
sources: Neil, Practical Vim 2e

title: DSA Foundations (Goodrich)
blurb: The theory track: a chapter-by-chapter tour of Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser - analysis, recursion, arrays, lists, trees, heaps, hashing, search trees, sorting, text, graphs and external memory - with runnable implementations and build-it-yourself exercises.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python (Wiley, 2013), ch. 3-15

title: Patterns I — Arrays, Hashing & Two Pointers
blurb: The first two NeetCode roadmap patterns, taught properly: how to attack an interview problem, hash maps from the inside out, prefix sums and counting tricks, and every flavour of two pointers.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 5 (Array-Based Sequences)
Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 10 (Maps and Hash Tables)
NeetCode roadmap (NeetCode 150 / 250)
CPython documentation and source notes on dict/set

title: Patterns II — Sliding Window, Stack & Binary Search
blurb: Three patterns that turn O(n²) and O(n) scans into O(n) and O(log n): sliding windows, (monotonic) stacks and deques, and binary search done right — including binary search on the answer.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python — ch. 4.1.3 (binary search), ch. 5.3 (amortization), ch. 6 (stacks, queues, deques)
NeetCode 150 roadmap
Python docs: bisect, collections.deque

title: Patterns III — Linked Lists, Trees & Tries
blurb: Pointer surgery on linked lists, every flavour of tree traversal, binary search trees and tries — the node-based half of the NeetCode 150, with a judge that builds the lists and trees for you.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 7 (linked lists), ch. 8 (trees), ch. 11 (search trees), ch. 13.5 (tries)
NeetCode 150 (Linked List, Trees, Tries)

title: Patterns IV — Heaps, Backtracking & Graphs
blurb: Priority queues and the top-k / two-heap patterns, the backtracking template with pruning, and the full graph toolkit: DFS/BFS, topological sort, union-find, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, MSTs and Eulerian paths — with 58 judged NeetCode problems.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 9 (Priority Queues)
Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 14 (Graph Algorithms)
NeetCode 150 roadmap

title: Patterns V — Dynamic Programming
blurb: From recursion trees to tables: the state / recurrence / base case / order / answer framework, then the NeetCode 1-D and 2-D DP problems plus knapsack, LIS, string, grid and interval DP.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 13.3 (Dynamic Programming)
NeetCode 150 roadmap — 1-D and 2-D Dynamic Programming

title: Patterns VI — Greedy, Intervals, Math & Bits
blurb: When the locally best move is globally right (and how to prove it), interval sweeps and meeting-room heaps, matrix and number-theory tricks, and bit manipulation with Python's unbounded integers.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python — §4.4 (repeated squaring), §13.4.2 (the greedy method), ch. 14 (greedy graph algorithms)
Bryant & O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective — ch. 2 (bit-level operations, two's complement, integer arithmetic)
NeetCode 150

title: SQL from Zero to Interview
blurb: Relational thinking and standard SQL from first SELECT to window functions, recursive CTEs and interview patterns - run every query live on six seeded datasets, then practise on 93 problems.
sources: Alan Beaulieu, Learning SQL (O'Reilly), ch. 1-15 and appendices
SQLite documentation (window functions, WITH clause, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN)
PostgreSQL and MySQL reference manuals (dialect notes)

title: Databases & Data-Intensive Systems
blurb: Storage engines, replication, partitioning, transactions, consensus, batch and stream processing - a chapter-by-chapter companion to Designing Data-Intensive Applications, plus practical databases for ML engineers.
sources: Martin Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications (O'Reilly, 2017), ch. 1-12
PostgreSQL documentation (postgresql.org/docs)
Redis documentation (redis.io/docs)
Apache Kafka documentation (kafka.apache.org/documentation)
Malkov & Yashunin, Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW graphs (2016)

title: MongoDB
blurb: Documents, CRUD, querying, indexes, aggregation, transactions, schema design, replication, sharding and operations - a chapter-by-chapter companion to MongoDB: The Definitive Guide, plus PyMongo, change streams, Atlas Vector Search for RAG and interview-style data-modelling exercises.
sources: Bradshaw, Brazil & Chodorow, MongoDB: The Definitive Guide, 3rd ed. (O'Reilly, 2019), ch. 1-24
MongoDB Manual (mongodb.com/docs/manual)
PyMongo and Motor documentation (pymongo.readthedocs.io, motor.readthedocs.io)
MongoDB Atlas Vector Search documentation (mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search)

title: Spring Boot
blurb: tmp
sources: tmp

title: Go (Learning Go)
blurb: Go from the first `go run` to production services: types, slices and maps, interfaces, generics, errors, modules, goroutines and channels, context, testing, the standard library and the runtime questions interviewers love. Written for complete beginners, with runnable simulations and practice problems.
sources: Jon Bodner, Learning Go: An Idiomatic Approach to Real-World Go Programming, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly), ch. 1-16 (topic coverage and fact-checking only; all wording and examples are original)
The Go Programming Language Specification, go.dev/ref/spec
Go documentation: Effective Go, the Go Memory Model, the Go blog and package docs, go.dev/doc and pkg.go.dev

title: FastAPI & Backend Engineering
blurb: From HTTP fundamentals to production APIs: FastAPI, Pydantic, dependencies, async, databases, auth, testing, streaming and deployment — ending with a complete ML model-serving service.
sources: Bill Lubanovic, FastAPI: Modern Python Web Development (O'Reilly, 2023)
FastAPI official documentation — https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/
Pydantic v2 documentation — https://docs.pydantic.dev/

title: JavaScript (Eloquent JavaScript)
blurb: The JavaScript language from values and closures to promises and the event loop, then the browser (DOM, events, canvas, fetch) and Node.js, with runnable examples, live pages and judged problems.
sources: Haverbeke, Eloquent JavaScript (4th ed.), ch. 1-21
MDN Web Docs (developer.mozilla.org)

title: TypeScript
blurb: From your first type annotation to conditional types: the type system, generics, configuration, real React and Node projects, and the questions interviewers ask. Explained from zero, with runnable examples.
sources: Josh Goldberg, Learning TypeScript (O'Reilly)
The TypeScript Handbook (typescriptlang.org/docs)

title: GraphQL & API Design
blurb: tmp
sources: Porcello & Banks, Learning GraphQL (O'Reilly, 2018)

title: Django
blurb: tmp
sources: tmp

title: Docker & Containers
blurb: Containers from the kernel up: namespaces, cgroups and layered images, Dockerfiles and the build cache, registries, storage, Compose, health checks, observability, Swarm and Kubernetes, safe upgrades, secrets, CI builds, multi-architecture images, security hardening, ML/GPU images and worked interview answers.
sources: Elton Stoneman, Learn Docker in a Month of Lunches (Manning, 2020), ch. 1-21
Official docs: docs.docker.com (Dockerfile reference, Compose file reference, Engine, Build, Swarm)
Official docs: kubernetes.io, prometheus.io, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, astral.sh/uv

title: CI/CD & Continuous Delivery
blurb: How software gets from a commit to production safely and repeatedly: continuous integration, deployment pipelines, test strategy, release patterns, infrastructure as code, database change, branching, DORA metrics - then hands-on GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker, Argo CD and worked interview scenarios.
sources: Jez Humble & David Farley, Continuous Delivery (Addison-Wesley, 2010), ch. 1-15
Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate / DORA State of DevOps research (four key metrics)
Official docs: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Argo CD, Argo Rollouts, OpenFeature, Semantic Versioning, Conventional Commits, trunkbaseddevelopment.com

title: Computer Networking for Engineers
blurb: From bits on a wire to HTTP/3: layers, IP and routing, TCP, DNS, TLS, wireless, HTTP, browser performance, real-time APIs and backend networking, explained from zero with runnable simulations, annotated tool output and interview-style problems.
sources: Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (https://hpbn.co)
MDN Web Docs (HTTP, Fetch, WebSocket, Performance APIs)

title: Web Application Security
blurb: Defensive security for developers, from zero: how the web works, how each class of vulnerability arises, vulnerable-versus-fixed code, layered defences, testing, threat modelling, the secure development lifecycle, LLM application security and interview-ready answers.
sources: Andrew Hoffman, Web Application Security (O'Reilly, 2020)
OWASP Top 10 — https://owasp.org/www-project-top-ten/
OWASP Cheat Sheet Series — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/
MDN Web Docs, Security on the web — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security

title: Open-Ended Engineering Questions
blurb: How to answer interview questions that have no single right answer: testing a product, updating a decision table, designing classes, APIs, schemas and systems, debugging from evidence, weighing trade-offs, planning, security, ML and behavioural stories. Reusable frameworks, fully worked answers, 230 practice questions and judged coding problems.
sources: ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level syllabus v4.0 (https://www.istqb.org)
Winters, Manshreck & Wright, Software Engineering at Google (https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book)
Beyer et al., Site Reliability Engineering (https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)
Martin Fowler and colleagues, articles on delivery, design and data (https://martinfowler.com)
Trunk Based Development (https://trunkbaseddevelopment.com) and DORA research (https://dora.dev)
Google API Improvement Proposals (https://google.aip.dev) and Google Engineering Practices (https://google.github.io/eng-practices/)
OWASP threat modelling, Top 10 and cheat sheets (https://owasp.org)
Donne Martin, System Design Primer (https://github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer); Yangshun Tay, Tech Interview Handbook (https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org)
Martin Zinkevich, Rules of Machine Learning (https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

title: Computer Systems & Architecture
blurb: How programs really run: bits and floats, x86-64 assembly, pipelined processors, caches, linking, processes and signals, virtual memory, I/O, sockets and threads, following CS:APP.
sources: Bryant & O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective, 3rd ed. (CS:APP 3e)

title: Operating Systems (Tanenbaum)
blurb: Processes, memory, files, I/O, deadlocks, virtualization, multiprocessors and security, with runnable simulations of every classic algorithm and two real-system case studies.
sources: Tanenbaum & Bos, Modern Operating Systems, 4th ed., ch. 1–12

title: Machine Learning
blurb: From the maths underneath to scikit-learn models, evaluation, pipelines, text, deep-learning essentials and interview-ready system design — with runnable code in every lesson and 25 numpy implementation problems.
sources: Müller & Guido, Introduction to Machine Learning with Python (O'Reilly), ch. 1–8
scikit-learn User Guide (scikit-learn.org)
Chip Huyen, AI Engineering (O'Reilly) — background for deep learning and system design
Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville, Deep Learning — background for the maths and optimisers

title: MLOps: From Notebook to Production
blurb: Take a model from a Jupyter notebook to a monitored, versioned, containerised, continuously delivered production service — data pipelines, experiment tracking, Docker, serving, Kubernetes, CI/CD/CT, drift monitoring, cost, and LLMOps.
sources: Chip Huyen, AI Engineering (O'Reilly, 2025), ch. 3-4 (evaluation), ch. 9 (inference optimization), ch. 10 (architecture & user feedback)
Martin Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, ch. 10-11 (batch and stream processing)
Bill Lubanovic, FastAPI (O'Reilly, 2023), ch. 12-13 (testing, production)
Mueller & Guido, Introduction to Machine Learning with Python, ch. 5-6 (evaluation, pipelines)
Sculley et al., Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems (NeurIPS 2015)
Official docs: MLflow, DVC, Docker, Kubernetes, KServe, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Evidently, Feast, Airflow, Prefect, BentoML, Ray Serve, vLLM, Hugging Face

title: AI Engineering (Chip Huyen)
blurb: Build real applications on top of foundation models: how they work, how to evaluate them, prompting, RAG and agents, finetuning, data, inference optimization and production architecture.
sources: Chip Huyen, AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models (O'Reilly, 2025), ch. 1-10

title: LLMs Hands-On: Transformers, Hugging Face, RAG, MCP & Context Engineering
blurb: The hands-on and internals companion to the AI Engineering track: build attention and BPE in numpy, drive the Hugging Face stack, ship RAG and LoRA fine-tunes, write MCP servers, and engineer context for long-running agents.
sources: Hugging Face LLM Course & Agents Course (huggingface.co/learn)
Hugging Face docs: Transformers v5, Tokenizers, Datasets, PEFT, TRL, Hub, TGI
Model Context Protocol specification 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25 (modelcontextprotocol.io)
Anthropic Engineering: Building effective agents; Effective context engineering for AI agents; Writing tools for agents
Chip Huyen, AI Engineering (O'Reilly, 2025), ch. 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10
Vaswani et al. 2017; Su et al. 2021 (RoPE); Hu et al. 2021 (LoRA); Dettmers et al. 2023 (QLoRA); Rafailov et al. 2023 (DPO)

title: React (with Firebase)
blurb: Modern React from the first component to how the reconciler works: state, effects, data fetching, forms, routing, testing and TypeScript, then a full Firebase back end (auth, Firestore, security rules, hosting). Every idea runs live in the page with a hand-written mini React, plus 30 judged problems.
sources: Wieruch, The Road to React
Wieruch, The Road to React with Firebase
react.dev (official React documentation)
firebase.google.com/docs (official Firebase documentation)
